mainTopic: Women whose time is enough (דיה שעתה): a woman who miscarried, a pregnant woman, a nursing mother, and an elderly woman, with a side discussion on the water of sprinkling
overview: The amud begins by finishing a question about a מפלת, a woman who miscarried. Does she get the pregnant woman's leniency that her impurity starts only from the moment she sees blood (דיה שעתה)? רב פפי and רב פפא give two answers, and רב פפא ties the rule to the heaviness a pregnant woman feels. רבי זירא uses that reason to rule that a woman who saw blood before her pregnancy was noticeable is impure backward like any woman. רבי יוחנן then proves from the woman in hiding that a pregnant woman need not check herself at her usual period time, because her blood has stopped. Next comes a ברייתא about a nursing mother. רבי מאיר says the leniency lasts as long as she nurses, because the blood turns into milk. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say it lasts a fixed 24 months, because her body is weakened. A side discussion about the פסוק 'Who can bring a pure thing out of an impure?' leads into the puzzling laws of the water of sprinkling, which even שלמה could not grasp. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה to define a זקנה and what 'close to her old age' means.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge: labor near birth is pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge it began earlier. Blood seen during labor close to a birth is declared pure by the תורה, so why should a miscarriage be treated differently?
steps.simpleTranslation: Labor pain close to a birth: the תורה declared it pure!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the גמרא in the middle of a question about a מפלת. Here it closes that question by pointing to the rule that blood seen during labor near a birth is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says blood seen during hard labor (קושי) right before a birth does not make a woman a זבה. The challenge is: if a miscarriage counts as a birth, the same leniency should apply to her. The next two steps answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard labor, the pains before giving birth
Close to the birth
"The Merciful One", a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה
Declared it pure

phrases.english: Labor pain close to the birth
the Merciful One declared it pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The treatment of the blood of a מפלת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood seen during labor near a real birth is pure by תורה law. If a miscarriage is like a birth, its blood should be treated the same way.

steps.title: רב פפי: the 24-hour rule is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי answers that the backward-reaching 24-hour impurity (מעת לעת) is only דרבנן, so we should not build a contradiction on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: Leave aside the twenty-four-hour period; it is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי answers the challenge. He says to set aside the 24-hour rule, because it is only a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that a miscarriage is not a real birth, so the תורה leniency for labor does not apply to her. The rule that impurity reaches back 24 hours was made by the רבנן, and they did not apply that extra stringency to a woman who miscarried. Since it is only דרבנן, it should not be used to raise a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside, put to one side
A 24-hour period. Normally a woman's impurity reaches back over the previous 24 hours.
From the Rabbis, not from the תורה

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
Leave aside the twenty-four-hour period, which is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: He means the rule that impurity reaches back 24 hours. Since it is only rabbinic, the Rabbis could choose not to apply it here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי: הַנַּח מֵעֵת לְעֵת דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrading the source of the law: the rule in question is only rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the miscarriage case must follow the תורה rules about birth and labor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 24-hour rule is דרבנן, so the Rabbis' leniency for a מפלת creates no contradiction with תורה law.

steps.title: רב פפא: her head and limbs were heavy here too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer. The reason a pregnant woman's "time is enough" is that her body feels heavy, and that was true during this pregnancy too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Isn't the whole reason only that her head is heavy on her and her limbs are heavy on her? Here too, her head and limbs are heavy on her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers another answer. He explains the reason behind the rule and shows that the reason fits a woman who miscarried as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We say a pregnant woman is טמאה only from now on because her body feels heavy, and this stops her regular flow, so we assume she did not bleed earlier. A woman who miscarried was also pregnant and felt that heaviness. So the same leniency applies to her, even if a miscarriage is not a full birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't the reason only...? A phrase that points to the true reason behind a rule
Her head feels heavy on her, the heaviness of pregnancy
Her limbs
Here too

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason (heaviness of the body) becomes the key that רבי זירא uses in the next question.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Is the reason anything
phrases.notes: Literally "Is the reason anything but...". It means "The only reason is..."

phrases.english: other than because her head is heavy on her
and her limbs are heavy on her?
Here too,
her head and limbs are heavy on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מִידִּי הוּא טַעְמָא אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּרֹאשָׁהּ כָּבֵד עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the rule so that it fits the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the leniency for a pregnant woman depends on her giving a proper birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency depends on the bodily heaviness of pregnancy, which a woman who miscarried also had.

steps.title: She saw blood before her pregnancy became noticeable
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא about a woman who saw blood and only later was her pregnancy noticeable. Is she טמאה backward like a regular woman?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: If she saw blood and afterward her fetus became noticeable, what is the law? Since at the time she saw, her fetus was not yet noticeable, she is impure. Or perhaps, since she saw close to that time, she is not impure?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question. A woman saw blood, and only afterward did people notice she was pregnant. Does she still get the pregnant woman's leniency?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has two sides. Since her pregnancy was not noticeable when she saw blood, maybe she is like any regular woman and is טמאה backward 24 hours. Or perhaps, since the blood came close to the time her pregnancy became noticeable, she already counts as pregnant and is not טמאה backward.

keyTerms.meaning: Her fetus became noticeable (her pregnancy became known)
What is the law?
She becomes impure
Or perhaps, which introduces the other side of a question

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:

phrases.aramaic: רָאֲתָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּכַּר עוּבָּרָהּ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If she saw blood, and afterward her fetus became noticeable, what is the law?
Since at the time that she saw
her fetus was not noticeable, she is impure;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דִּסְמִךְ לַהּ חֲזַאי —
phrases.english: or perhaps, since she saw close to it,
phrases.notes: "Close to it" means close to the time her pregnancy became noticeable.

phrases.english: she is not impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the משנה's rule for a pregnant woman
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the pregnant woman's leniency apply when she saw blood before her pregnancy was noticeable, if it became noticeable soon after?

steps.title: רבי זירא: at that time she did not feel heavy, so she is impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers using the reason behind the rule. When she saw the blood, she did not yet feel the heaviness of pregnancy, so she is טמאה backward like any woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Isn't the whole reason only that her head and limbs are heavy on her? At the time she saw, her head was not heavy on her and her limbs were not heavy on her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. He points back to the reason for the leniency and shows that it was missing when she saw the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency exists only because a pregnant woman's body feels heavy, which stops her flow. When this woman saw blood, she did not yet feel that heaviness. So the reason does not apply, and she is טמאה backward like a regular woman.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time
That she saw (blood)
"Her time is enough": she is impure only from the moment she sees blood, not backward

steps.whatToRemember: The pregnant woman's leniency is tied to the physical heaviness of pregnancy. A woman who miscarried had it, so she gets the leniency (רב פפא). A woman who saw blood before her pregnancy was noticeable did not yet have it, so she does not get the leniency (רבי זירא).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא's opening words are a question in form, but they are really a statement: "the only reason is the heaviness." He is not unsure. He is using the reason to decide the case.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Is the reason anything
other than because her head is heavy on her
and her limbs are heavy on her?
At the time that she saw,
her head is not heavy on her
and her limbs are not heavy on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידִּי הוּא טַעְמָא אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּרֹאשָׁהּ כָּבֵד עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is טמאה backward like a regular woman, because at the time she saw blood she did not yet feel the heaviness of pregnancy, which is the whole reason for the leniency.

steps.title: Must a pregnant woman check herself at her usual period time?
steps.stepSummary: An elder asks רבי יוחנן what happens if a pregnant woman's usual period time comes and she did not check herself. He asks only according to the view that וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder asked רבי יוחנן: If the time of her usual period came while she was pregnant, and she did not check herself, what is the law? I am asking only according to the one who says that the rules of fixed periods are from the תורה. Do we say that since they are from the תורה, she must check? Or do we say that since her blood has stopped during pregnancy, she does not need to check?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. An elder wants to know if a pregnant woman must check herself when her usual period time arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If וסתות are only דרבנן, the question is easy: she would not need to check. The elder therefore asks only on the view that they are דאורייתא. On that view there are two sides. A Torah rule might require a בדיקה no matter what, or the fact that a pregnant woman's blood has stopped might cancel the need.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's fixed, expected time for her period
The days of her pregnancy
A self-check to see if blood came out
The view that the rules of fixed periods are from the תורה
Her blood has stopped (it is not expected to come)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: A certain elder asked Rabbi Yochanan:
If the time of her fixed period arrived during her pregnancy
and she did not check herself, what is the law?
I am asking this
according to the one who says fixed periods are from the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דִּוְסָתוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה,
phrases.english: What is it? Since fixed periods are from the Torah, she needs a check,
or perhaps, since her blood has stopped,
she does not need a check?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about pregnancy, linked to the earlier theme that a pregnant woman's blood has stopped.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a בדיקה required for a pregnant woman at her וסת time, on the view that וסתות are דאורייתא?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן cites the woman in hiding
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers from רבי מאיר's ruling. A woman in hiding who did not check at her וסת is טהורה because fear stops the blood. Without fear, she would be טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this. רבי מאיר says: If she was in hiding, and the time of her period came, and she did not check, she is pure, because fear stops the blood. The reason is that there is fear. But if there is no fear, and her period time came, and she did not check, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a source to answer the question. He first reads a precise inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes her טהורה only because of the fear. That means a normal woman who skips her בדיקה at her וסת time is טמאה. This shows the וסת rule has real force, yet it can be cancelled when we know the blood has stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (the answer is in a known source)
A hiding place (hiding from danger)
Fear stops the flow of blood
The reason is X, which implies that without X the law is different

phrases.english: He said to him: You already learned it:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיְתָה בְּמַחֲבֵא
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: If she was in hiding
and the time of her period came and she did not check,
she is pure, because fear stops the blood.
The reason is that there is fear,
but if there is no fear
and her period time came and she did not check, she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the elder's question by bringing a source and drawing an inference from it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר's ruling shows that a woman who skips her בדיקה is normally טמאה, but is טהורה when something known to stop the blood is present.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר on the woman in hiding (מחבא)

steps.title: Pregnancy is like fear: no check needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן concludes that רבי מאיר holds וסתות are דאורייתא, yet fear removes the need for a בדיקה. A pregnant woman's blood has also stopped, so she does not need to check either.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that fixed periods are from the תורה. Still, since there is fear, her blood has stopped and she does not need a check. Here too, with a pregnant woman, her blood has stopped and she does not need a check.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן applies the source to the elder's case. A pregnant woman does not need to check at her usual period time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making her טמאה without a בדיקה shows that רבי מאיר treats וסתות as דאורייתא, which is exactly the view the elder asked about. Even on that view, fear cancels the need to check because the blood has stopped. Pregnancy works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / this shows

steps.whatToRemember: Even if וסתות are דאורייתא, a woman whose blood is known to have stopped does not need a בדיקה at her usual time. This applies to fear, and also to pregnancy.

phrases.english: So we see that fixed periods are from the Torah,
and still, since there is fear,
her blood has stopped, and she does not need a check.
Here too, her blood has stopped,
and she does not need a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוחנן's proof and applies it to pregnancy.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A pregnant woman who did not check at her וסת time is טהורה, because her blood has stopped, even on the view that וסתות are דאורייתא.

steps.title: A nursing mother whose baby died is like all women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a nursing woman and brings a ברייתא. If her baby died within 24 months, she loses the leniency and is like all women regarding מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A nursing woman, until she weans, and so on. The Sages taught: A nursing woman whose child died within twenty-four months is like all women. She makes things impure back twenty-four hours, and back from one check to the last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, about a nursing mother, and brings a ברייתא on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a nursing woman the leniency of דיה שעתה. This first ruling is רבי מאיר's view (the ברייתא names him in the next step): the leniency depends on actual nursing, so if the baby died she goes back to the normal backward-reaching impurity. The sages in step 11 disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: A nursing mother
Until she weans the baby
She makes things impure going back a full 24 hours
Going back to her last self-check

phrases.english: A nursing woman, until she weans, etc.
The Sages taught: A nursing woman whose child died
within twenty-four months
is like all women,
and she makes things impure back twenty-four hours and back to her last check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה, the nursing woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a nursing woman whose baby died within 24 months loses דיה שעתה and is טמאה מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה like other women.

steps.title: Nursing for four or five years keeps the leniency
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: since the leniency follows actual nursing, a woman who keeps nursing for four or five years still has דיה שעתה. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if she kept nursing him for four or five years, her time is enough. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws the other side of the same rule. Longer nursing means a longer leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לפיכך shows that this follows from the first half. The leniency follows the nursing itself, not a fixed 24-month calendar. So just as it ends early when the baby dies, it continues past 24 months while she still nurses.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore (this follows from what was just said)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, a nursing woman's leniency depends on whether she is actually nursing, not on the 24-month count. It ends if the baby dies, and it lasts as long as she nurses.

phrases.english: Therefore, if she was nursing him
and kept going for four or five years,
her time is enough. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same ברייתא, drawing a consequence from the first half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a woman who nurses for four or five years keeps דיה שעתה for that whole time.

steps.title: The other view: the leniency lasts only 24 months
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say a nursing woman has דיה שעתה for 24 months only. If she nurses for four or five years, then after 24 months she is like all women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: their time is enough for a full twenty-four months. Therefore, if she nursed him for four or five years, she makes things impure going back twenty-four hours, or back to her last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and brings the opposing view to רבי מאיר. These three sages tie the leniency to a fixed 24 months, not to actual nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the leniency lasts as long as she actually nurses. Here the leniency is set by time: 24 months from birth. After that she loses it, even if she is still nursing.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-four months, the fixed period of the leniency in this view
She makes things impure (here, going back in time)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
their time is enough
for a full twenty-four months,
therefore, if she was nursing him
for four or five years —
she makes things impure going back twenty-four hours
or back to her last check.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nursing leniency lasts a fixed 24 months. After that she is like all women, even if she keeps nursing.

steps.title: The reason behind each view
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that the blood turns into milk. The other sages hold that her body is weakened and does not recover until 24 months.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you come to explain it: according to רבי מאיר, the blood breaks down and becomes milk. According to רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, her limbs come apart, and her strength does not return until twenty-four months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why each side ruled the way it did. Each reason fits its ruling exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood turns into milk, the leniency should last as long as she makes milk, which means as long as she nurses. That is רבי מאיר. If her body is weakened by the birth, the leniency depends on recovery time, which is 24 months, whether she nurses or not. That is the other sages.

keyTerms.meaning: When you come to explain it: introduces the reasons
The blood breaks down and becomes milk
Her limbs come apart, meaning her body is weakened
Her strength, her normal state

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: blood becomes milk, so the leniency follows nursing. רבי יוסי and the others: the body is weakened, so the leniency follows a fixed 24 months.

phrases.english: When you come to explain it,
according to Rabbi Meir —
the blood breaks down and becomes milk,

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן —
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yosei, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon —
her limbs come apart,
and her strength does not return
phrases.notes: נפש here means her strength and normal body cycle, not her soul.

phrases.english: until twenty-four months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two rulings in steps 10 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the blood becomes milk. The other sages: her body is weakened for 24 months.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר need his 'therefore' clause?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר spelled out the case of nursing four or five years, since it is obvious from his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need רבי מאיר's 'therefore'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר's 'therefore' clause is needed at all. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's reason is that blood becomes milk. So it is obvious that the leniency lasts as long as she nurses, even for years. Adding 'therefore, even four or five years' seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? Asks why a line is needed if it seems obvious

phrases.english: The 'therefore' of Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: This is the line from step 10: since it follows nursing, even nursing for four or five years keeps the leniency.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 12 to question whether רבי מאיר's clause in step 10 is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the extra 'therefore' clause in רבי מאיר's view add?

steps.title: It is there only to match רבי יוסי's clause
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's 'therefore' adds nothing new. It was said only to match the 'therefore' in רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of רבי יוסי's 'therefore'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר's clause really is not needed for its own sake. The ברייתא added it so his view would match the shape of the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits the line is extra. Since רבי יוסי's side has a 'therefore' clause, the ברייתא gave רבי מאיר's side a matching one.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of

phrases.english: Because of the 'therefore' of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר's clause is extra. It is said only to match רבי יוסי's clause.

steps.title: Why does רבי יוסי need his 'therefore' clause?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי's clause is needed, since his reason of 24-month recovery seems to make it obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need רבי יוסי's 'therefore'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question on רבי יוסי's clause. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason is that her body needs 24 months to recover. So it seems obvious that after 24 months she loses the leniency, even if she still nurses. The question is what his clause adds.

phrases.english: And the 'therefore' of Rabbi Yosei
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question as step 13, now about רבי יוסי's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the 'therefore' clause in רבי יוסי's view add?

steps.title: So we do not think רבי יוסי holds both reasons
steps.stepSummary: Without the clause, one might think רבי יוסי also agrees that blood becomes milk. The clause shows that after 24 months she loses the leniency even while nursing, so his only reason is the weakened body.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יוסי holds two reasons. So the clause teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי's clause is truly needed. It makes clear that he holds only one reason, not both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought רבי יוסי holds both reasons: her body is weakened, and her blood also becomes milk. Then a woman still nursing after 24 months would keep the leniency. The 'therefore' clause says she becomes impure going back in time after 24 months, which proves he holds only the reason of the weakened body.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces a mistaken idea
He holds two (reasons)
It teaches us: shows why the line is needed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's 'therefore' is just there to match the other view. רבי יוסי's 'therefore' is truly needed: it shows he holds only the reason of the weakened body, so the leniency ends at 24 months.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think both clauses are extra. Only רבי מאיר's is there for matching. רבי יוסי's teaches a real point.

phrases.english: You might have said
that Rabbi Yosei holds two reasons,
so it teaches us that he does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי תַּרְתֵּי אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause shows that רבי יוסי holds only the reason of the weakened body. So after 24 months she loses the leniency even while nursing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי holds both reasons, so the leniency would continue as long as she nurses.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי holds only one reason, so the leniency ends at 24 months.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the explanation of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states the dispute in the same terms as the explanation already given: רבי מאיר says blood becomes milk, and רבי יוסי says her limbs are weakened for 24 months.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: the blood spoils and becomes milk, says רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says her limbs come apart, and her strength does not come back until 24 months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what was explained earlier about the two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 12 the גמרא explained the two reasons on its own. Now a ברייתא says the same thing word for word, so that explanation is backed up by an older source. Nothing new is added; the explanation is simply confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way: a ברייתא that backs up what was just said
spoils or breaks down
her strength does not come back to her

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a ברייתא):
The blood spoils and becomes milk,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Her limbs come apart,
and her strength does not return to her
until twenty-four months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports, from a ברייתא, the explanation of the two reasons given in Step 12 and sharpened in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that רבי מאיר's reason is blood turning into milk, and רבי יוסי's reason is a weakened body for 24 months.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating both opinions in those exact terms.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי says רבי מאיר learns his idea from the פסוק 'Who can bring a pure thing out of an impure? Is it not the One?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: What is רבי מאיר's reason? Because it is written: 'Who can bring a pure thing out of an impure? Is it not the One?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי gives a פסוק as the source for רבי מאיר's idea that impure blood can become pure milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from her flow is impure, but milk is pure. The פסוק says that only the One, meaning ה׳, can make something pure come out of something impure. רבי מאיר reads this as describing blood turning into milk.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?
something pure coming out of something impure
is it not the One? Meaning ה׳

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?
As it is written: "Who can bring a pure thing out of an impure?
Is it not the One?"
phrases.notes: Meaning ה׳ can do it. Here the impure blood becomes pure milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַאי: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source verse for the opinion of רבי מאיר just quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's idea that blood becomes milk comes from 'Who can bring a pure thing out of an impure?'

steps.title: How do the other Sages read this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר explain the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages? How do they explain this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the other Sages do with this פסוק, since they do not use it for blood turning into milk. This question sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Sages do not hold that blood becomes milk, the פסוק must be teaching them something else. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages? Short for: how do the other Sages explain this?

phrases.english: And the Sages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing Sages read the verse that רבי מאיר used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the Sages who reject 'blood becomes milk' learn from the פסוק 'Who can bring a pure thing out of an impure?'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the verse is about שכבת זרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that, for the Sages, the פסוק refers to שכבת זרע. It is impure, yet the person formed from it is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is שכבת זרע, which is impure, and yet the person formed from it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the Sages' reading of the פסוק: a pure person comes from impure שכבת זרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages still read the פסוק as 'pure from impure', but they apply it to a different example. So the פסוק does not prove that blood turns into milk.

keyTerms.meaning: semen, which makes a person impure
who is formed from it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is semen, which is impure,
and the person formed from it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to a pure person coming from impure שכבת זרע.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the verse is about מי הנדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the פסוק refers to the water of sprinkling. The one who sprinkles it and the one sprinkled on are pure, yet one who touches it is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: This is the water of sprinkling. The one who sprinkles and the one it is sprinkled on are pure, but one who touches it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second answer: the 'pure from impure' in the פסוק is about the water of sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same water purifies the person it is sprinkled on, yet it makes impure someone who touches it. That strange mix of pure and impure is what the פסוק marvels at. This is a different answer from רבי יוחנן's.

keyTerms.meaning: the water of sprinkling, mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
one who sprinkles
the one the water is sprinkled on
one who touches

steps.confusionAlert: Here מי הנדה does NOT mean anything about a נדה woman. It is the name of the purifying water made with the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
These are the waters of sprinkling,
phrases.notes: This is the water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה, not anything about a נדה woman.

phrases.english: for the one who sprinkles and the one sprinkled upon are pure,
and one who touches is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ מֵי הַנִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 19, different from רבי יוחנן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to the water of sprinkling, which purifies some people but makes the one who touches it impure.

steps.title: But the תורה says the sprinkler washes his clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. How can the sprinkler be pure, when the פסוק says the one who sprinkles must wash his clothes?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the one who sprinkles really pure? But it is written: 'He who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's claim that the one who sprinkles stays pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing clothes is a sign of impurity. So the פסוק seems to say the sprinkler becomes impure, which goes against רבי אלעזר's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? Used to raise a challenge from a פסוק
he shall wash his clothes, a sign of impurity

phrases.english: And is the one who sprinkles pure?
But it is written: "And he who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:21. The same פסוק goes on: 'and he who touches the water... is impure until evening.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 21 that the sprinkler is pure.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the מזה is pure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק requires the מזה to wash his clothes, which shows he is impure.

steps.title: 'מזה' in the verse means one who touches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'מזה' in the פסוק really means one who touches the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he who sprinkles' mean? He who touches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר by reading the word 'מזה' in the פסוק as someone who touches the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is talking about someone who touches, then the actual sprinkler is not being made impure. That keeps רבי אלעזר's statement that the sprinkler is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: What does 'מזה' mean here?

phrases.english: What is "he who sprinkles"? One who touches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מזה' means the person actually sprinkling, so he is impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מזה' means one who touches the water, so the real sprinkler stays pure.

steps.title: 'מזה' cannot mean one who touches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. The פסוק mentions both 'מזה' and 'נוגע' separately, and it gives the מזה a stricter law (washing clothes) than the נוגע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says 'he who sprinkles' and it also says 'he who touches'! And besides, the one who sprinkles must wash his clothes, while the one who touches does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer that 'מזה' means one who touches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the same פסוק names both people, so they cannot be the same person. Second, they have different laws: only the מזה washes his clothes. So 'מזה' must be someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore, adding a second objection
washing of clothes, a sign of more serious impurity
requires

phrases.english: But it is written "he who sprinkles,"
and it is written "he who touches"!
And furthermore, "he who sprinkles" requires washing (of clothes),
while "he who touches" does not require washing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists both terms separately and gives them different laws, so they cannot mean the same person.

steps.title: 'מזה' means one who carries the water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'מזה' in the פסוק means one who carries the water. That explains why he must wash his clothes while the real sprinkler stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'he who sprinkles' mean? One who carries.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of 'מזה': a person who carries the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying makes a person more seriously impure than touching, so the carrier must wash his clothes. This fits the פסוק and still lets the actual sprinkler be pure, so רבי אלעזר's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, bringing a new answer after the old one fell
one who carries

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר, the water of sprinkling is a 'pure from impure' case. The sprinkler and the one sprinkled on are pure, the one who touches is impure, and the 'מזה' who washes his clothes is really one who carries the water.

phrases.english: Rather, what is "he who sprinkles"?
One who carries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after Step 24 rejected the reading in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מזה' means one who carries, who needs to wash his clothes. The real sprinkler stays pure.

steps.title: Why not just write 'one who carries'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'מזה' really means one who carries the water, the תורה should simply have written 'נושא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the תורה write 'one who carries'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If the פסוק means a carrier, why use the word for a sprinkler?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said 'מזה' means one who carries the water. But the תורה has a clear word for carrying, 'נושא'. Using 'מזה' instead needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it write

phrases.english: But let it write 'one who carries'!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק in במדבר 19:21, which says 'מזה' even though, by step 25, it means a carrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording behind step 25's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'מזה' as 'one who carries'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תורה meant carrying, it should have used the plain word for carrying.

steps.title: Only carrying enough water for a sprinkling makes one impure
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מזה' teaches that the carrier only becomes טמא if he carries at least the amount needed for a הזאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that he is not impure until he carries the amount needed for sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'מזה' was chosen on purpose. It sets the amount a carrier must carry to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נושא' alone would make any amount of carrying count. Saying 'מזה' links the carrying to sprinkling: only a הזאה-sized amount makes the carrier טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Carries
The amount needed for one sprinkling

phrases.english: It teaches us
that it is only when he carries the measure of sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by giving the word 'מזה' a purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra meaning drawn from the chosen word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'מזה' seemed wasted if the פסוק means a carrier.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מזה' sets the minimum: carrying a הזאה's worth of water.

steps.title: What about the view that sprinkling needs no minimum?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the view that הזאה needs a שיעור, but not for the view that it needs none.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says sprinkling needs a measure. But for the one who says it needs no measure, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 27. There is a view that a הזאה has no minimum amount, so how could 'מזה' teach a minimum?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 depends on a 'measure of sprinkling' existing. If any tiny drop is enough for a הזאה, there is no such measure, and the answer seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
Needs a minimum amount
What can be said?

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
sprinkling requires a measure,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: but according to the one who says it does not require a measure,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הַזָּאָה צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 27 from the other opinion about a שיעור for הזאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of a 'measure of sprinkling' in step 27
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If הזאה has no minimum, there is no measure for 'מזה' to teach.

steps.title: No minimum on the person, but a minimum in the vessel
steps.stepSummary: Even the view that הזאה needs no שיעור only means the amount landing on the person. The vessel must still hold a set amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the one who says it needs no measure means only on the man's body. But in the vessel, we need a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both views agree there is a minimum. They only disagree about the water that lands on the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any drop on the טמא person may be enough. But the vessel the sprinkler dips into must hold a real amount, and that is the 'measure of sprinkling' the carrier must carry.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to
On the body of the man
A vessel
We require

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different amounts here: what lands on the person, which may have no minimum, and what sits in the vessel, which always has one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: Even according to the one who says it does not require a measure,
that applies only to the back of the man,
phrases.notes: 'The back of the man' just means the body of the person being sprinkled.

phrases.english: but in the vessel, we require a measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by limiting where the 'no measure' view applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'no measure' view seemed to deny any measure for הזאה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only removes the minimum on the person; the vessel still needs a set amount.

steps.title: The משנה about how much water the vessel needs
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מסכת פרה gives the minimum water in the vessel: enough to dip the tips of the stems and sprinkle.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: How much water must be there so it is enough for sprinkling? Enough to dip the tips of the stems and sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that the vessel needs a minimum amount of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks how much water makes 'enough for sprinkling' and gives a real amount. This proves the vessel has a שיעור, backing up step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough for sprinkling
He will dip
The tips of the stems of the אזוב

phrases.english: As we learned: How much must be in the water
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת פרה (12:5).

phrases.english: so that there will be enough in it for sprinkling?
Enough that he can dip the tips of the stems and sprinkle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 29 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the vessel used for הזאה requires a minimum amount of water

steps.title: Even שלמה could not fully understand this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the topic with שלמה's words: 'I said I would become wise, but it is far from me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what שלמה said: 'I said I would become wise, but it is far from me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole discussion of מי חטאת. It says this is the kind of law that even שלמה המלך found beyond him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same water makes a טמא person טהור, yet makes the people handling it טמא. This strange mix is what שלמה meant when he said wisdom was far from him.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is
I will become wise
It is far from me

steps.whatToRemember: The 'מזה' in the פסוק means one who carries a הזאה's worth of water; the real sprinkler stays טהור. The vessel always needs a set amount of water, even for the view that the person needs no minimum.

phrases.english: And this is what Shlomo said:
'I said, I will become wise,
but it is far from me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole מי חטאת side discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The laws of מי חטאת are so puzzling that even שלמה said their wisdom was far from him.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: who counts as an elderly woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a זקנה is a woman who went three עונות without seeing blood, close to her old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is an elderly woman? Any woman who has passed three cycles close to her old age.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its definition of a זקנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a זקנה is a woman who missed three עונות without seeing. The added words 'close to her old age' are the phrase the גמרא will now ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: An elderly woman
Expected periods (cycles)
Close to her old age

phrases.english: Who is an elderly woman?
Any woman for whom three cycles have passed
[close to her old age].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected text; the גמרא asks about exactly these words next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מי חטאת topic and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקנה is a woman who went three עונות without seeing blood, close to her old age.

steps.title: What does 'close to her old age' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to define 'close to her old age'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'close to her old age'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what point in a woman's life counts as 'close to her old age'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses this phrase without explaining it. The גמרא wants a clear test for when it applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How is it defined?
Her old age

phrases.english: What is considered close to her old age?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a phrase from the משנה in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of 'close to her old age'

steps.title: רב יהודה: when her friends call her old
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says it is any woman whose friends say about her, 'She is old.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: Any woman whose friends say about her, 'She is an elderly woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question with a practical test: how other women see her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה does not give a fixed age. He uses common opinion: if her friends call her old, she is 'close to her old age'.

keyTerms.meaning: Her friends
They say about her

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
Any woman about whom her friends say
'She is an elderly woman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Close to her old age' is when her friends say she is old.

steps.title: רבי שמעון begins a different definition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to bring רבי שמעון's view on the same question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון says:
